source.title: Orbitofrontal cortex is required for optimal waiting based on decision confidence

confidence_rationale: A causal inactivation study whose central result cuts BOTH ways for ARC-055 and is the most decision-relevant finding in this pull. It supports the claim's explicitness requirement -- the confidence representation is anatomically separable enough that removing one region abolishes confidence-guided behaviour -- while directly complicating the claim's assertion that the signal must be available to SELECTION, since decision accuracy survived the same inactivation intact. Confidence 0.60 reflects a well-executed causal manipulation whose bearing on the claim is genuinely two-directional rather than uncertain.
failure_signatures: ARC-055 asserts V(t) must be available to and influence E3 trajectory selection. Here, inactivating the region that carries the explicit confidence signal disrupted the confidence-guided waiting report while leaving decision accuracy unaffected -- i.e. the selection ran without the explicit signal. If REE's E3 selection is analogous, the availability requirement is stronger than this preparation demonstrates and may be architecturally optional rather than mandatory.

An alternative reading that would rescue the claim -- that choice in this task uses an implicit graded evidence quantity while only the REPORT needs the explicit signal -- is exactly the epiphenomenon/explicit-signal distinction ARC-055 turns on, and this experiment does not adjudicate it. The claim's key architectural commitment is therefore left undetermined rather than confirmed.

Task-scope limit: a two-alternative perceptual decision has a trivial trajectory space, so 'decision accuracy unaffected' may not generalise to selection over extended trajectories where a depth-like criterion would actually have work to do.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In a temporal wagering task in which rats express decision confidence through how long they wait for a delayed reward, orbitofrontal cortex inactivation disrupts waiting-based confidence reports without affecting decision accuracy, identifying orbitofrontal cortex as supporting metacognitive confidence judgments separately from the perceptual decision mechanism itself.
mapping.ree_translation: ARC-055 makes two joined assertions: that V(t) and D_V are explicit signals, and that they are available to and influence E3 selection as well as E1/E2 learning. This experiment separates those two assertions and returns different verdicts. On explicitness it is supportive and unusually strong evidence: a signal that can be causally removed by inactivating one region, with a specific and selective behavioural consequence, is by construction an addressable representation rather than a diffuse property of the computation. On availability-to-selection it is awkward. The choice itself was unimpaired by the very manipulation that abolished confidence-guided behaviour, which is the pattern one expects if selection is driven by an implicit graded quantity and the explicit signal serves other consumers. Read against ARC-055, this is a live challenge to the necessity of the E3 leg -- not a refutation, because the alternative reading (implicit evidence drives choice, explicit confidence drives report and learning) is itself a coherent architecture, but a demonstration that the claim's E3 leg has to be argued rather than assumed.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The strongest caveat runs against reading this as a refutation. A two-alternative perceptual choice has essentially no trajectory structure, so it is a poor test bed for a claim about selection among extended trajectories evaluated over a horizon; a depth-like signal would have nothing to contribute to accuracy in this task even if it were architecturally mandatory in a richer one. Equally, inactivation removes a region, not a signal: OFC carries much besides confidence, and preserved accuracy is evidence that the choice circuit was intact, not that it never reads confidence. Species and task scope (rat, sensory two-alternative, wagering readout) are a substantial extrapolation to REE's E3.
mapping.source_context: Rats in a temporal wagering task with confidence expressed as waiting duration for delayed reward; pharmacological/optogenetic inactivation of orbitofrontal cortex with decision accuracy measured concurrently.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality 0.85: Neuron, a causal manipulation rather than a correlation, with the critical control (decision accuracy) measured in the same animals under the same inactivation -- the dissociation is internal, not across studies. Mapping fidelity 0.65: the explicitness leg maps well, the selection leg maps onto a task whose trajectory space is degenerate. Transfer risk 0.40. Aggregate 0.60, set by the two-directional bearing rather than by any weakness in the experiment; the entry is filed 'mixed' precisely so governance sees the tension rather than a net-of-signs number.
